title: Project Ledger Web
description: Financial dashboard for managing projects, teams, and monthly project cash flow, with modules for operations, collaboration, reporting, billing plans, and workspace-based organization.

bts.title: Product Scope and Operational Modules
bts.body: The app currently includes authentication flows, monthly KPI dashboards, complete project finance modules (expenses, incomes, categories, obligations, budgets, partners, settlements, and members), reports with Excel/PDF export, billing plans, workspace grouping, and an integrated chatbot in the protected shell.

bts.title: Architecture and Technical Approach
bts.body: Built with Next.js App Router and route groups for auth/dashboard, using thin pages that delegate to views, centralized route protection by role, a shared API client (refresh, cancelation, GET dedup, typed errors), domain services, and orchestration hooks for complex project-detail coordination.

lessons.title: Domain-Driven Frontend Structure Scales Better
lessons.body: Using the page → view → hooks → services pattern keeps pages lightweight and allows business features to grow without inflating routing layers or creating coupling between modules.

lessons.title: Strong Foundations Expose the Next Maturity Step
lessons.body: Centralized HTTP behavior and i18n-by-feature improved consistency and maintenance speed. The next logical improvements are stronger unit coverage for hooks/services, deeper observability, and more advanced reporting hardening.

title: Project Ledger API
description: Multi-tenant backend built with ASP.NET Core 10 and PostgreSQL, deployed on Azure free tier. Powers expenses, incomes, obligations, budgets, OCR-assisted drafts, AI-related workflows, and Stripe billing integration.

bts.title: Azure + PostgreSQL Deployment
bts.body: Deployed the API to Azure free tier while keeping PostgreSQL as the main data store, balancing cost constraints with a stable backend environment for ongoing feature work.

bts.title: Core Financial + OCR Flow
bts.body: Implemented and connected core finance modules with OCR-assisted transaction drafts so users can capture document data first and validate before it impacts totals.

lessons.title: Strong C# and .NET Foundations
lessons.body: This project helped me improve a lot in C# and .NET, especially around API structure, clean layering, and writing more maintainable backend code.

lessons.title: Clean Code Improves Delivery
lessons.body: Applying cleaner practices and better organization made feature delivery smoother as the API grew to include OCR, billing, and AI-related integrations.

title: CineMatch Backend
description: NestJS + Firebase backend for CineMatch, focused on secure authentication, movie and series interactions, social features, and recommendation flows inspired by cinematic preference patterns.

bts.title: Modular NestJS Architecture
bts.body: Structured backend modules around auth, users, media, lists, friends, and recommendations, making responsibilities explicit and easier to scale as the platform grew.

bts.title: Firebase Sync + Social Core
bts.body: Implemented Firestore-backed synchronization and social interactions including activity tracking, user media actions, and real-time behavior needed by the CineMatch experience.

lessons.title: Clear Backend Boundaries Improve Quality
lessons.body: Designing each responsibility as a dedicated module improved maintainability and made endpoint behavior easier to reason about as features evolved.

lessons.title: Security and Recommendation Logic Must Coexist
lessons.body: I strengthened auth and API protection while implementing recommendation-related flows, learning to balance product features with secure backend practices.

title: CineMatch
description: Mobile social app for movie lovers with user matching by film taste, real-time chat powered by Firebase, forums, and TMDB integration.

bts.title: Taste-Based Matching
bts.body: Implemented matching logic focused on connecting users with similar movie preferences to strengthen community discovery and interaction quality.

bts.title: Firebase Real-Time Chat
bts.body: Implemented Firebase-powered real-time messaging for matched users, enabling responsive conversations as a core social feature of the app.

lessons.title: Mobile Best Practices Matter
lessons.body: This project helped me improve my mobile development practices, especially around cleaner architecture, reusable components, and scalable feature organization.

lessons.title: Scalability Starts Early
lessons.body: As social features expanded, I learned to keep code quality high from the start so new capabilities can be added without destabilizing the app.

title: SGI Avalom
description: Complete property administration platform for rentals, contracts, clients, payments, accounting visibility, and operational control across buildings and units.

bts.title: Property and Rental Operations
bts.body: Built modules for buildings, properties, clients, rentals, and payment flows to replace spreadsheet-heavy processes with a centralized web system.

bts.title: Accounting and Reporting
bts.body: Added dashboards, filtering, and export-ready reporting to improve financial supervision and day-to-day administration for property managers.

lessons.title: Domain-Driven Modules Improve Maintainability
lessons.body: Structuring the app by real operations (rentals, accounting, clients, properties) made it easier to extend features without creating coupling between unrelated areas.

lessons.title: Business Workflows Need Clear Data Boundaries
lessons.body: The project reinforced the importance of consistent data models and lifecycle states for contracts and payments in systems with operational and financial impact.

title: Colyseus Multiplayer
description: Multiplayer backend for Whispers in the Woods, my first 3D game project in PlayCanvas. Handles real-time sync, room events, and matchmaking for a 1v1 horror experience.

bts.title: First 3D Game Journey
bts.body: This was my first full 3D game project, from initial concept and art direction to implementation, which made the development process both challenging and fun.

bts.title: Multiplayer Implementation
bts.body: Implemented the multiplayer layer with Colyseus to keep both players synchronized in real time, handling room events and gameplay state updates.

lessons.title: Building a Game from Zero Is Different
lessons.body: Designing a game from scratch required learning beyond code, including concept planning, iteration flow, and close alignment between design and implementation.

lessons.title: Real-Time Multiplayer Is a Great Teacher
lessons.body: Working on multiplayer synchronization taught me practical lessons about state handling, event timing, and debugging interactive systems.

title: ClinicaUNA
description: JavaFX medical record and appointment system connected to Payara and Oracle 21c XE, with multilingual support (Spanish/English), role-based access, and Jasper Reports.

bts.title: Complete Clinic Workflow
bts.body: Implemented end-to-end modules for users, doctors, patients, appointments, and medical records, including schedule handling, consultation history, and follow-up data capture.

bts.title: Reporting and Operations
bts.body: Integrated Jasper Reports plus dynamic reporting capabilities to generate agenda and patient history outputs, supporting administrative and clinical operations.

lessons.title: Enterprise Structure in Desktop Apps
lessons.body: I learned to handle larger business workflows in JavaFX by organizing modules around real clinic processes and maintaining clear separation between UI, service, and persistence layers.

lessons.title: Data Accuracy Is Critical in Health Systems
lessons.body: Building medical and appointment flows reinforced the importance of validation, role permissions, and consistent data handling when software supports sensitive operations.

title: Proyecto Pac-Man
description: Enhanced Pac-Man built in JavaFX with dynamic mazes, advanced ghost pathfinding (A*, BFS, DFS, Dijkstra), power-ups, trophies, and 10 themed levels.

bts.title: Advanced Ghost AI
bts.body: Implemented multiple pathfinding behaviors for ghost personalities and difficulty settings, creating varied and more challenging gameplay.

bts.title: Dynamic Gameplay Systems
bts.body: Added random maze generation, power-ups, trophies, stats, and save/load flow to extend the classic Pac-Man loop into a richer game experience.

lessons.title: Game Feel Depends on Systems Working Together
lessons.body: Balancing movement, AI behavior, scoring, and power-up timing taught me that small gameplay systems must be tuned as a whole, not in isolation.

lessons.title: Feature-Rich Games Need Strong Structure
lessons.body: As mechanics grew, organizing code by responsibilities became essential to keep iteration speed high and avoid regressions.

title: Tours Control
description: JavaFX tourism management desktop app with map-based route visualization, 3D image carousel, drag-and-drop assets, billing workflows, and PDF invoice generation.

bts.title: Map and Route Visualization
bts.body: Implemented itinerary visualization with interactive mapping to show route stops and improve tour planning clarity for users.

bts.title: Billing and Operations
bts.body: Built tour billing flow with PDF export and support utilities like searchable maintenance modules and drag-and-drop media management.

lessons.title: Desktop UX Still Demands Product Thinking
lessons.body: Working on this project reinforced that desktop tools also need smooth workflows, discoverable controls, and clear visual hierarchy.

lessons.title: Complex Modules Benefit from Shared UI Patterns
lessons.body: Reusing interaction and form patterns across maintenance views helped reduce inconsistencies and improve long-term maintainability.

title: Monopoly Junior
description: Digital Monopoly Junior implementation in JavaFX with interactive board gameplay, property and bank management, chance cards, and save/load support.

bts.title: Interactive Board Mechanics
bts.body: Implemented turn-based board interactions including dice flow, tile actions, property purchases, rent handling, and chance-card effects.

bts.title: Game State and Persistence
bts.body: Added player economy and state management with save/load functionality so sessions could continue without losing progression.

lessons.title: Board-Game Logic Needs Clear Rules Modeling
lessons.body: I learned to model game rules explicitly to avoid ambiguous states and keep turns, transactions, and outcomes predictable.

lessons.title: Persistence Is Part of User Experience
lessons.body: Supporting saved sessions highlighted how important state recovery is for playability in longer game loops.

title: Chrome Dev Assistant
description: Chrome extension that automates debugging prompt workflows by capturing developer error input and sending structured prompts through configurable modes.

bts.title: Prompt Workflow Automation
bts.body: Built an extension flow where users paste errors, choose a workflow mode, and trigger automated prompt handling to speed up debugging iterations.

bts.title: Lightweight Developer UX
bts.body: Designed a straightforward popup interface in React and Tailwind so developers can quickly configure context and send prompts without leaving their browser workflow.

lessons.title: Developer Tools Need Fast Interaction Loops
lessons.body: I learned that tool adoption depends heavily on reducing friction and keeping each action path short and predictable.

lessons.title: Clear Prompt Structure Improves Outcomes
lessons.body: Providing consistent workflow options and context inputs helps produce better responses and a more repeatable debugging process.
